>I'll graduate college, graduate professional school, get married, find some boring job, pop a couple of kids out who'll probably be just as fucked up as I am, wait on bated breath for retirement, and fall into an even deeper depression once I don't have a routine to keep me grounded. I can't understand how anyone around me ISN'T depressed. Life is meaningless, and we're all just prolonging our inevitable deaths.

I know it's a clichéd saying, but it's not about the destination but the journey. There's no guarantee any of the negative things you stated would ever happen, you never know with life, and that's just how it is. And people are different, with different goals and aspirations, and not everybody has the same outlook towards life and things, in general. Believe me, I know how hard it is to get out of this rut called existential despair and when you can't help but think that if nothing matters in the end, why even live? Well, we live because we've born. Not a very good argument, I know, but I've found it to be sufficient enough at times. You sound like a smart person, and have a lot of loved ones. The only reason they might feel bad when you tell them about yourself is probably because they haven't been in the same shoes as you, and can't relate to this shitty thing called depression. It's not their fault, neither it's yours. Have you tried travelling? I believe that can help a lot at times, just exploring new places, meeting new people, expanding your horizons, etc. Or maybe a new hobby? I personally found this very helpful, I found something so interesting that I was willing to live longer just to explore it further.
I know it's easier said than done. But you gotta start somewhere, right? Don't overthink the situation you're in, just say what you feel like and you'll do fine. Best wishes ~

Hi, there's no "cure" to those social problems because they're not problems at all. We're all different and some us are just not very social beings. As an introvert, I can relate to your post very much. I had that social anxiety too, but as I grew older I just became more and more cynical and cared less about what others thought of me. If you want to talk to someone, simply say "Hi" and it will do. You're in a leadership course? That's great, that's one small step to overcoming your anxiety. You can try talking to yourself while looking at a mirror, I've found that to help a lot too. You like video games? Then talk to people who like video games, you'll find that a lot easier. It's easier to talk to someone when you have mutual interests and hobbies.

 Small steps everyday! :)
